discovered_patterns.pattern_name: Encrypted, per-user, gateway-side response cache with header control
evidence: The gateway automatically caches results and reuses them when possible.
Cache encryption The gateway uses AES-GCM to encrypt the cache, using a key derived from your API key.
Because the cache’s encryption key is your API key, cached results are scoped to an individual user. Braintrust customers can opt into sharing cached results across users within their organization.

Configure gateway behavior with these headers:- x-bt-use-cache: auto | always | never - x-bt-cache-ttl: Seconds (max 604800) ... The gateway returns the x-bt-cached header in the response with HIT or MISS
discovered_patterns.description: A gateway-level caching layer with fine-grained header-driven controls (modes, TTL) and encrypted storage scoped by the API key (AES-GCM). Cache modes and explicit headers let clients control whether to read/write cache and set TTL; cache hits are surfaced via response headers.
discovered_patterns.why_notable: Deriving an encryption key from the user's API key to ensure that cached responses are only decryptable by that user is an uncommon privacy-preserving design in model gateways; it provides strong isolation while retaining the performance and cost benefits of caching.

unique_findings: Privacy-first, per-client encrypted response cache: the gateway encrypts cached LLM responses with a key derived from the caller's API key (AES-GCM). This makes cached outputs unreadable to Braintrust and scopes cached results to the originating user unless org-level sharing is explicitly enabled.

OpenAI-compatible multi-provider gateway that performs provider-agnostic translation: the gateway accepts OpenAI-style requests and can route them to Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, Vertex, Azure, etc., letting teams use one client surface to exercise multiple backends (including custom/self-hosted models).

Deterministic caching heuristic tied to model parameters: 'auto' cache mode caches only when requests are deterministic (temperature=0 or seed set) and only for supported endpoints (/chat/completions, /embeddings, /completions, /moderations), preventing accidental cache usage for non-deterministic calls.

Prompt-as-first-class deployable artifact with versioning and environment pinning: prompts edited in the UI immediately affect production by default, but SDKs support pinning to a specific version ID and selecting environment-assigned versions (dev/staging/production) to control rollout.

Local prompt compilation API (build/load without execution): the SDK can compile prompt templates to messages, model, and params without calling an LLM (build()), enabling offline validation, local testing, or re-use with third-party LLM clients.

Deep tracing + observability integration with user-controlled logging: instrumentation auto-captures inputs/outputs, tokens/costs, nested spans and supports OpenTelemetry, x-bt-parent header for distributed traces, and SQL queryable logs + evaluation tooling (autoevals, scorers, aggregate scores).

Flexible credential scoping: organization-level provider keys are defaults but project-level keys override them (set by x-bt-project-id). This matches complex enterprise needs for billing/isolated usage without changing client code.

Rich runtime controls via custom headers (x-bt-*): caching, TTL, org/project selection, endpoint selection, logging parent span, and span metadata can be toggled per-request without SDK changes — enabling runtime experimentation and debugging.

Automations and online scoring: rules can sample production logs, run selected scorers, and attach continuous/categorical/free-form human review scores — embedding evaluation and QA into live traffic.

Cross-language, full-stack SDK and tooling ecosystem: SDKs (TS, Python, Java, Go, Kotlin, Ruby, C#), CLI, SQL query layer for logs, Loop analytics, and UI features (span iframes, tag/score config) tie runtime behavior to developer workflows and governance.

story_angles.headline: Braintrust’s gateway: one OpenAI‑compatible façade for every model — and the plumbing that makes it work
story_angles.summary: A deep dive into Braintrust’s provider-agnostic gateway: an OpenAI‑style surface that routes to Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, self‑hosted models and more, with project‑level credential overrides, custom provider plumbing, and OpenAI SDK compatibility for surprising cross‑provider tricks. This angle unpacks the tradeoffs of an OpenAI‑compatible API layered over heterogeneous backends and why that matters for engineers building multi‑provider stacks.
evidence: Gateway exposes an OpenAI-compatible facade and supports many providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, AWS Bedrock, Vertex, Azure, Baseten, Groq, Mistral, etc.)
OpenAI SDK can be used to call Anthropic/Claude models; base URL differences for Gemini noted
Project-level AI provider keys override organization defaults; supports custom providers and self‑hosted models

story_angles.headline: Braintrust’s privacy-first cache: AES‑GCM encrypted LLM responses that Braintrust claims it can’t read
story_angles.summary: Braintrust encrypts gateway cache entries with AES‑GCM using a key derived from the user’s API key so cached responses are scoped to individual users and—by design—unreadable by Braintrust. For developers and compliance teams, this raises novel questions about HIT rates, reproducibility, key rotation, and multi‑user sharing of cached results.
evidence: Cache encryption: gateway uses AES‑GCM; key derived from your API key; cached results scoped to an individual user
Caching modes and headers: x-bt-use-cache (auto/always/never), x-bt-cache-ttl, x-bt-cached: HIT/MISS; default TTL 1 week

story_angles.headline: They bet on server‑side prompt versioning and environment pinning — deliberately keeping control away from models
story_angles.summary: Rather than pushing model/version control or experimentation entirely to client logic, Braintrust enforces prompt versioning, environment pinning, and a build() compilation step that lets developers test locally without invoking models. This is a contrarian posture compared with approaches that treat models as mutable infra; it prioritizes reproducibility and safer production rollouts at the cost of some operational flexibility.
evidence: Every prompt save creates a new version with a unique ID; invoke() can pin specific versions; environments (dev/staging/production) select assigned versions
build() compiles a prompt template locally without making an API call, useful for testing and using messages with your own LLM client

story_angles.headline: How Braintrust tries to cut model spend: header‑driven caching, deterministic cache rules, and per‑request TTLs
story_angles.summary: The gateway provides fine‑grained, header‑driven caching (auto/always/never), TTL controls, and automatic reuse of responses to reduce provider calls. This angle evaluates where those controls can deliver big savings (low‑temperature, deterministic requests) and where they might fail (agentic, stateful, or privacy‑sensitive flows).
evidence: Cache modes (auto/always/never) with auto using temperature=0 or seed and restricted paths (/chat/completions, /embeddings, /completions, /moderations)
Cache‑control integration, x-bt-cache-ttl header, and gateway returning x-bt-cached and Age headers; default cache TTL one week

"Braintrust cannot see your data and does not store or log API keys. Because the cache’s encryption key is your API key, cached results are scoped to an individual user." — focuses on privacy-by-design but not on unique data assets.

anti_patterns.description: Some claims may overstate guarantees or imply stronger protections than are fully documented (e.g., absolute privacy/security or that Braintrust cannot access cached results), and marketing language occasionally presents broad capability without technical depth tied to measurable guarantees (SLA, threat model, compliance).
evidence: "This design ensures that the cache is only accessible to you. Braintrust cannot see your data and does not store or log API keys."
"The gateway is designed for production workloads, and uptime is tracked on the Braintrust status page" — but no SLA or specific uptime guarantees are provided in the excerpt.
Repeated, high-level claims like "Complete TypeScript ecosystem" and "Complete Python ecosystem" without demonstration of exclusive functionality or scale.

anti_patterns.description: The market for multi-provider gateways, SDKs, and observability for LLMs is crowded; many incumbents and cloud providers are building similar features. Without clear vertical focus, unique workflows, or enterprise lock‑in, positioning risks being generic.
evidence: Features overlap with offerings from cloud providers and other gateway/orchestration products (multi-provider support, caching, telemetry, SDKs, CLI, SQL).
The product surface (SDKs, API, CLI, SQL, UI) is broad but not obviously vertically specialized or uniquely positioned.

competitors.name: LangSmith (by LangChain Labs)
competitors.similarity: Provides LLM observability, tracing, prompt / chain debugging, prompt versioning and run history; integrates into developer workflows targeting LLM apps.
competitors.how_different: Braintrust bundles observability with an AI gateway (multi-provider proxy with caching and encryption), built-in prompt deployment/invoke semantics, richer evaluation tooling (human review scores, aggregate scores, online scoring rules) and first-class SDKs across many languages and frameworks. Braintrust emphasizes production tracing (spans, tokens, costs) and integrations (OpenTelemetry, LangChain) plus project-level provider keys and cache encryption tied to API keys.

competitors.name: PromptLayer / PromptOps-type tools
competitors.similarity: Track prompts, prompt histories and versions; help developers debug prompt behavior and reproduce runs.
competitors.how_different: PromptLayer focuses on prompt logging and analytics. Braintrust adds an execution gateway (proxy + provider abstraction), prompt deployment with version pinning and environments, built-in evaluation pipelines, human-in-the-loop labeling, and automatic span-based traces linking prompts to parent app traces.

competitors.name: Weights & Biases (W&B) / Neptune.ai
competitors.similarity: General ML experiment tracking, logging, metrics, model evaluation and dashboards for reproducibility and model performance monitoring.
competitors.how_different: W&B is broader ML experiments and not LLM-first. Braintrust is LLM- and agent-native (captures tokens, model params, spans for LLM calls, prompt rendering, agent steps), provides gateway-level provider orchestration and caching, plus prompt-level deploy/invoke workflow and specialized evaluation primitives (scorers, automations, sample/online scoring).

competitors.name: Fiddler AI / Arthur.ai (ML monitoring & explainability)
competitors.similarity: Model monitoring, explainability, drift detection and governance for production models.
competitors.how_different: Fiddler focuses on model governance/explainability for classical ML and some model types. Braintrust centers on LLM observability, distributed traces of LLM calls and agents, prompt management, integrated human review workflows and an AI gateway to unify providers — features tailored to LLM app development and iteration rather than classic model explainability.

competitors.name: Datadog / OpenTelemetry-based observability stacks
competitors.similarity: Application tracing, distributed spans, metrics, logs and dashboards; integration with OpenTelemetry.
competitors.how_different: Datadog/OpenTelemetry provide general observability but not LLM-specific capture (tokens, model params, prompt-level semantics) or prompt/version management, multi-provider gateway, built-in scoring and evaluation datasets. Braintrust integrates LLM semantics into traces (LLM calls, tokens, costs, prompt templates) and couples observability with evaluation tooling.

competitors.name: Hugging Face (Inference API + Model Hub) & Baseten-type model deployment platforms
competitors.similarity: Unified access to many models/providers, hosted inference, custom model deployments and endpoints.
competitors.how_different: Hugging Face and Baseten are model hosting/inference platforms. Braintrust positions a gateway/proxy that unifies existing commercial providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Bedrock, etc.) and self-hosted models, adds caching, per-request provider selection, logging into traces, and project-level provider overrides — plus the observability + evaluation layer tightly integrated with prompt management.

differentiation.primary: A combined LLM-native observability + prompt management + multi-provider gateway that unifies provider access, production tracing, evaluation automation, and prompt deployment/versioning — all integrated into developer SDKs and instrumented traces.
differentiation.technical: Key technical differentiators include: a gateway/proxy that is OpenAI-client compatible (can call Anthropic/Gemini via OpenAI SDK mappings), request-level caching with AES-GCM encryption keyed to the user's API key (scoped and optionally org-shared caches), deep tracing model (traces/spans capturing LLM inputs/outputs, tokens, costs, nested tool/agent steps), prompt build() to compile messages locally, versioned prompts and environment pinning, and broad SDK & framework integrations (LangChain, OpenTelemetry, LangChain SDK adapters, many language SDKs).
differentiation.business: Business differentiators include: developer-first workflows (invoke(), pinning prompt versions, immediate UI-to-production changes), project-level provider keys for billing/isolation, flexible pricing tiers for teams to enterprises, a beta/free gateway to onboard users, and product breadth that spans evaluation (human review, aggregate scores, online scorers) through to production routing and caching.
differentiation.positioning: Braintrust positions itself not just as monitoring or experiment tracking but as the operational layer for LLM apps — the place where prompts are authored, deployed, executed against many providers, observed, annotated, and evaluated end-to-end. It frames itself versus generic observability tools and single-provider tooling by being LLM-native and provider-agnostic.

secret_sauce.core_advantage: An integrated stack that combines a multi-provider, OpenAI-compatible gateway (with provider abstraction, caching and privacy-focused encryption), LLM-first distributed tracing (spans capturing tokens, params, nested agent/tool steps), and built-in evaluation workflows (human review, scorers, automations, dataset building) — all tied into developer SDKs and prompt deployment/versioning.
secret_sauce.defensibility: Medium. Defensibility comes from: deep integration into customers' runtime (instrumentation hooks and tracing that capture production signals), developer workflows and repos of versioned prompts/environments (switching cost), labeled evaluation datasets and human-review workflows accumulated in-platform, and the gateway’s encryption/scoping model which makes cached results private to API keys and optionally sharable within orgs. These create product lock-in through operational and data artifacts. However many components (tracing, gateways, caching) have plausible substitutes and competing vendors and open-source projects can replicate parts of the feature set.
evidence: Gateway supports many providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, AWS Bedrock, Vertex, Azure, Mistral, etc.) and allows custom providers and self-hosted models.
Gateway automatically caches results, returns x-bt-cached: HIT or MISS, supports TTL, and encrypts cache with AES-GCM using a key derived from your API key so cached results are scoped to the user.
Prompts are versioned on every save; code can invoke prompts via invoke() and pin versions in production; build() compiles prompt templates without calling a model.

Instrumentation captures inputs/outputs, model parameters, timing, tokens and costs, nested function/tool calls, and integrates with frameworks (LangChain, OpenTelemetry) and many SDKs (TypeScript, Python, Java, Go, Kotlin, Ruby, C#).
Project-level controls: project-level AI provider keys, project analytics (Loop to compare project metrics), online scoring rules and automated sampling for production logs.

competitive_analysis.moat_explanation: Braintrust’s moat is driven by developer workflow lock-in (versioned prompts, environments, invoke integration into code), deep runtime instrumentation that becomes part of customers’ production observability, and built-up labeled evaluation datasets and human-review processes. The gateway's caching/encryption model and provider-agnostic orchestration reduce friction for customers wanting to switch providers. However, individual components (tracing, caching, gateway proxy) are not deeply proprietary and can be replicated by large observability vendors, cloud providers, or open-source tools; competitors also move fast in the LLM tooling space. Thus the moat is meaningful but not impregnable.

evidence_quotes: Prompts created in Braintrust can be called directly from your application code. Changes made in the UI immediately affect production behavior, enabling rapid iteration without redeployment.
Use invoke() to call a deployed prompt by its slug

The Braintrust gateway ( https://gateway.braintrust.dev/v1 ) is currently in beta and free to use. It is designed for production workloads, and uptime is tracked on the Braintrust status page under AI Gateway.

The gateway supports Standard providers include:- OpenAI (GPT-5.2, GPT-5-mini, GPT-5-nano, etc.) - Anthropic (Claude 4.6 Sonnet, Claude 4.6 Opus, Claude 4.5, etc.) - Google (Gemini 3.0 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Pro, etc.) - AWS Bedrock (Claude, Llama, Mistral models) - Vertex AI (Gemini, Claude models) - Azure OpenAI (GPT-5.2, GPT-5-mini, GPT-5-nano, etc.) - Additional providers (Baseten, Fireworks, Groq, Mistral, etc.)

Braintrust integrates with all major AI providers and frameworks:- AI Providers: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Mistral, Together, Groq, and many more - Agent Frameworks: Claude Code, LangGraph, CrewAI, Autogen, Pydantic AI, and many more - SDK Integrations: LangChain, OpenTelemetry, Vercel AI SDK, LlamaIndex, DSPy, and many more
AES-GCM cache encryption where the key is derived from the user's API key, scoping cached results to the user by default (opt-in sharing across orgs).
Unified gateway design that allows OpenAI-compatible SDKs to call other providers (e.g., using OpenAI SDK to call Anthropic/Gemini) enabling SDK-level portability across backends.

Header-driven per-request behavioral controls (x-bt-use-cache, x-bt-cache-ttl, x-bt-project-id, x-bt-parent, x-bt-endpoint-name, x-bt-span-metadata) to control caching, logging, routing, and telemetry without code changes.
Cache heuristics that auto-cache only deterministic requests (temperature=0 or seed present), plus cache modes (auto|always|never) and TTL controls per-request.

Prompt versioning and environment pinning (pin version IDs, separate dev/staging/prod prompt assignments) allowing UI-driven prompt changes with immediate production effects and ability to pin stable versions.

Integrated trace/span model that treats prompts and provider calls as nested spans, combined with automatic logging and the ability to attach x-bt-parent to correlate gateway calls into distributed traces.
